The test image shows dense white cottony mycelium at the stem/crown base with small round yellowish sclerotia scattered throughout. This is highly characteristic of a soilborne fungal pathogen.

Key features:
- Dense white fluffy mycelium covering stem tissue
- Small spherical tan/yellow sclerotia (mustard-seed sized)
- Stem crown/base affected

This pattern strongly suggests **Southern Blight** (Sclerotium rolfsii) — the small round sclerotia are diagnostic. Now I'll view one reference image to confirm.

The reference image confirms Southern Blight with white mycelium on the stem at the crown. The test image is a close-up showing the same disease with the diagnostic small round yellowish sclerotia of *Sclerotium rolfsii* clearly visible embedded in the white cottony mycelium — a hallmark feature that distinguishes Southern Blight from Sclerotinia (which has larger, irregular black sclerotia).

Sclerotinia would produce larger irregular dark sclerotia, ruling out Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot."}
